thread:
alex: Heads-up — saw a surprising regional hit-rate delta after last night's runtime push. eu-west prefix cache hit-rate dropped to ~12% while us-east stayed ~68%.
priya: Yikes. Which part of the push? kernel selection, batching, or keying?
alex: kernel-selector change + a small cache-key tweak. We pinned `kernel_v2` for quantized transform-x and also started including `model_variant` in the cache key.
marco: hmm. Kernel pin was to improve long-seq throughput right? Could that affect KV layout/serialization?
alex: Exactly. Profiler shows a lot more KV evictions in eu-west and many miss paths fall back to host lookup. Example logs:
```
[2026-03-17T02:48:13Z] prefetch: evict=422 keyspace=prefix-kv eu-west
[2026-03-17T02:48:13Z] kernel: chosen=kernel_v2_quantized abi=kv-buckets-v2
[2026-03-17T02:48:13Z] kv: read_failure format_mismatch
```
sam: Could replication/coherency be interacting? If replicas differ by kernel/abi they might write different bucket formats.
alex: That's what it looks like. Routing sometimes lands requests on a replica with old runtime (kv-buckets-v1). New writes use v2 format and old readers can't interpret -> higher miss rate.
priya: We added `model_variant` to prevent cross-variant contamination during rollouts. That was intentional, but maybe it amplified key entropy and evictions in cold regions.
marco: Two concerns: (1) ABI change for KV buckets across kernel versions, (2) increased key cardinality from extra key field causing faster eviction on small regional caches.
sam: Proposal: rollback kernel pin on the next canary, add an explicit `kv_fmt` version header into the cache key (so different formats don't collide), and run a short rekey job for hot prefixes in eu-west.
alex: +1. Also add a compatibility shim so readers accept both bucket formats for ~24h to avoid hard misses.
priya: I can add the cache-key header change in the API layer (small patch). marco, can you prototype a dual-read shim in runtime?
marco: yes, I'll mock a try-v1 then v2 read path and benchmark overhead.
sam: I'll open INF-1293 and attach perf traces. infra-bot: rollback scheduled at 1723460000 unless blocked.
alex: Test matrix I want: seq lengths [16, 128, 1024], batch patterns (single vs burst), and routed-to-same-kernel vs cross-kernel replicas. Measure prefix hit-rate, p50/p90/p99 latency, and eviction rate.
priya: If eu-west hit-rate recovers above ~55% and p99 latency improves by >10% we can promote. Also consider temporarily biasing routing to same-kernel replicas for 12h while fix rolls out.
marco: One more tweak: reduce the effective TTL for newly salted keys in cold regions to avoid flooding small caches during rollout.
alex: Agreed. I'll draft the rollout playbook in the ticket with measurements and rollback steps.
priya: Thanks — this explains the odd latency spikes we saw in support dashboards.
sam: +1 for incremental fixes. No objections.
marco: will push a prototype by EOD.
alex: Thanks everyone. I'll paste the spike traces and raw logs into INF-1293.
infra-bot: Note: INF-1293 created and assigned to sam, alex, marco. Canary window: 1723462000-1723465600.
